Prioritization of the risk/opportunity to be addressed (materiality to interested parties; what needs to be addressed).
Whether baselines for water-related aspects/impacts/conditions are established as reference points for comparison of performance.
Whether the baseline reference is absolute or normalized (using variables affecting water use/consumption/quality).
Whether the evaluation of risks and opportunities is reviewed and updated routinely (manage change), especially after context/process/facility changes.
Whether appropriate actions to address identified water aspects/impacts/conditions/risks/opportunities have been determined (range of options considered).
Type of action selected (environmental objective, operational control, support action, performance action); may be combined.
Whether specific, relevant, achievable environmental objectives consistent with policy and significant aspects/risks have been established.
Level of the environmental objective (strategic, tactical or operational).
Whether related targets are measurable and time-bound (objectives should be achievable and include such targets).
Nature of the target related to the objective (qualitative/quantitative; absolute/relative).
Whether necessary support is provided (resources, competence, awareness, communication, documented information).
Whether the competence of persons doing work under the organization's control is determined, developed and maintained.
Whether persons doing work under the organization's control are aware of how their work can affect water use/consumption/quality and their role in achieving objectives.
Whether water-related documented information is established and controlled so processes/actions are controlled and intended outcomes achieved.
Whether relevant operational controls are applied to reduce variability, achieve intended outcomes and enhance performance.
Type of control in the hierarchy applied (elimination/substitution = source/pollution prevention; engineering/administrative = how operations are implemented).
Whether operational controls are applied with regard to a life cycle perspective over stages the organization has control or influence.
Whether the organization plans for water-related emergency situations (identify situations, determine risks, identify affected uses, establish/ test/review response plans).
Type of water-related emergency situation identified.
Whether the effectiveness of the emergency response plan(s)/procedure(s) is tested and reviewed at planned intervals.
Type of performance action planned (monitoring/measurement, observation/inspection, analysis/evaluation/audit).
Whether the organization evaluates if and to what extent actions taken (water withdrawal/use/quality, aquatic ecosystems) are effective.
Whether the organization has decided what/when/who/which methods/what data quality and how data are analysed for monitoring and measurement.
Whether the necessary data quality for monitoring/measurement is defined.
Whether all actions taken are reviewed in a timely manner for unintended consequences (which can be delayed, esp. groundwater) and addressed as appropriate.
Whether relevant fundamental indicators of performance / KPIs are identified and tracked to compare current state with baseline/target.
Whether the indicator is leading (expected/in-process performance, 3.10) or lagging (past/outcome performance, 3.11).
Form of KPI measurement (simple/absolute, relative/normalized, composite/index).
Whether the organization addresses gaps/nonconformities (causes, corrections, corrective actions) and implements opportunities for improvement.
Whether identified nonconformities, including their causes, are addressed with corrections and corrective actions.
Person oder Personengruppe mit eigenen Funktionen, Verantwortlichkeiten und Befugnissen (Begriff 3.1.4).

Relevante externe Themen einschliesslich Umweltzustaende und Ereignisse, die Taetigkeiten/Produkte/Dienstleistungen beeinflussen (Sec.4.1 a; Kasten 1: politisch, wirtschaftlich, rechtlich, natuerlich usw.).
Relevante interne Themen (Sec.4.1 a; Kasten 3: Fuehrung/Struktur, Einhaltung von Gesetzen, Politiken/Ziele/Strategien, Kapazitaet/Leistungsvermoegen, Kultur, Vertraege).
Umweltzustaende, die die Organisation beeinflussen koennen, einschliesslich Ereignisse (Kasten 2), z. B. klimabedingte Temperaturaenderung, Ueberschwemmung.
Personen/Organisationen, die eine Entscheidung/Taetigkeit beeinflussen, davon beeinflusst sein oder sich beeinflusst fuehlen koennen (Begriff 3.1.6, Sec.4.2.2).

label_de: Erfordernisse und Erwartungen relevanter interessierter Parteien
label_en: Needs and expectations of relevant interested parties
description: Bestimmte relevante Erfordernisse und Erwartungen der relevanten interessierten Parteien (Sec.4.2.3).

label_en: Scope of the environmental management system
description: Grenzen und Anwendbarkeit (physisch, funktional, organisatorisch) des UMS; als dokumentierte Information aufrechterhalten und interessierten Parteien zur Verfuegung gestellt (Sec.4.3).
Betrachtung der Steuerung und Einflussnahme ueber die Phasen des Lebenswegs (Sec.4.1, 4.3, Kasten 12).

label_de: Verpflichtung zum Schutz der Umwelt in der Politik
label_en: Policy commitment to protection of the environment
description: Die Umweltpolitik sollte die Verpflichtung zum Schutz der Umwelt einschliesslich Verhindern von Umweltbelastungen umfassen (Sec.5.2, Kasten 7).

label_de: Nachweis der Verpflichtung der obersten Leitung
description: Oberste Leitung uebernimmt Rechenschaft fuer die Wirksamkeit des UMS und stellt physische/finanzielle Ressourcen und Ausrichtung bereit (Sec.5.1).

Strategische Ausrichtung mit Verpflichtung zu Erfuellung bindender Verpflichtungen, Schutz der Umwelt, Verhindern von Umweltbelastungen und fortlaufender Verbesserung; als dokumentierte Information aufrechterhalten und kommuniziert (Sec.5.2).
Umweltpolitik allen Personen unter Aufsicht der Organisation mitgeteilt und interessierten Parteien zur Verfuegung gestellt (Sec.5.2).
Oberste Leitung weist Vertreter/Funktionen mit ausreichender Befugnis, Bewusstsein, Kompetenz und Ressourcen zu; Verantwortlichkeiten definiert und kommuniziert (Sec.5.3, Kasten 9).
Verstehen der Taetigkeiten, Produkte und Dienstleistungen, deren Bestandteile mit der Umwelt in Wechselwirkung treten koennen (Sec.6.1.2.2).
Bestandteil der Taetigkeiten/Produkte/Dienstleistungen, der mit der Umwelt in Wechselwirkung tritt oder treten kann (Begriff 3.2.2); Liste/Verzeichnis ueber Lebensweg (Sec.6.1.2.3).
Umweltaspekt, den die Organisation lenken bzw. unter Beruecksichtigung des Lebenswegs beeinflussen kann (Sec.6.1.2.3).

enum_values.label_de: Umweltaspekt, den die Organisation lenken kann
Umweltaspekt, den die Organisation beeinflussen kann

description: Veraenderung der Umwelt, ob unguenstig oder guenstig, die ganz oder teilweise aus Umweltaspekten resultiert (Begriff 3.2.4, Sec.6.1.2.4).
Der gewaehlte Ansatz sollte positive (nuetzliche) wie negative (schaedliche) Umweltauswirkungen erkennen koennen (Sec.6.1.2.4).

label_en: Criteria for determining significant environmental aspects
description: Festgelegte Kriterien (Aspekt: Typ/Groesse/Haeufigkeit; Auswirkung: Ausmass/Schwere/Dauer/Exposition) zur konsistenten Bewertung der Bedeutung (Sec.6.1.2.5).
Optionale qualitative Einstufung der Bedeutung (Beispiel verbatim 'hoch, mittel, niedrig oder vernachlaessigbar'); die Organisation kann eigene Skala/Schwellenwert festlegen (Sec.6.1.2.5).
Aspekt, der nach den Bedeutungskriterien als bedeutend bestimmt wurde; Eingabe fuer Politik, Ziele, Schulung, Steuerung, Ueberwachung (Sec.6.1.2.5).

label_de: Risiko bzw. Chance, die zu beruecksichtigen ist
label_en: Risk or opportunity that needs to be addressed
description: Aus den drei Quellen (Umweltaspekte, bindende Verpflichtungen, Themen aus 4.1/4.2) ermittelte Risiken und Chancen, die zu beruecksichtigen sind (Sec.6.1.1, Begriff 3.2.11).
Im Anwendungsbereich des UMS bestimmte moegliche Notfallsituationen, die Umweltfolgen haben koennen (Sec.6.1.1; weitere Anleitung Sec.8.2).
Rechtliche Verpflichtungen, die die Organisation erfuellen muss, und weitere Anforderungen, die sie erfuellen muss oder freiwillig erfuellt (Begriff 3.2.9, Sec.6.1.3.1).
Rechtliche Verpflichtung (Sec.6.1.3.2) oder weitere Anforderung (Sec.6.1.3.3).

label_en: Origin of the compliance obligation (interested party)
description: Ursprung einschliesslich der relevanten interessierten Partei (Sec.6.1.3.4, Aufzaehlungspunkt 1 des Verzeichnisses).

label_de: Bezug der Verpflichtung zu Umweltaspekten / Anforderungen
label_en: Relation of obligation to aspects / requirements
description: Wie die bindende Verpflichtung mit den Umweltaspekten und/oder relevanten Anforderungen interessierter Parteien zusammenhaengt (Sec.6.1.3.4).
Dokumentierte Information ueber bindende Verpflichtungen in Form eines Verzeichnisses oder einer Liste, regelmaessig ueberprueft (Sec.6.1.3.4).
Massnahme zur Behandlung bedeutender Umweltaspekte, bindender Verpflichtungen sowie Risiken und Chancen; technologische, finanzielle, betriebliche Anforderungen beruecksichtigt (Sec.6.1.4).
Die Organisation sollte die Wirksamkeit der ergriffenen Massnahmen bestimmen (Sec.6.1.4; Methoden vgl. 9.1).
Von der Organisation in Uebereinstimmung mit der Umweltpolitik festgelegtes Ziel (Begriff 3.2.6); auf relevanten Ebenen/Funktionsbereichen festgelegt (Sec.6.2.2).
Detaillierte Leistungsanforderung zur Erreichung eines Umweltziels; wenn festgelegt, sollte sie messbar sein und ggf. einen Zeitrahmen haben (Sec.6.2.2).
Wenn Einzelziele festgelegt werden, sollten sie messbar sein (Sec.6.2.2).
Programm mit Rollen, Verantwortlichkeiten, Prozessen, Ressourcen, Zeitrahmen, Prioritaeten und Massnahmen (Sec.6.2.3).
Festgelegte Kennzahl, die objektive, nachweisbare und reproduzierbare Ergebnisse liefert, geeignet fuer Taetigkeiten/Produkte/Dienstleistungen (Sec.6.2.4).
Umweltzustands- (ECI), Management- (MPI) oder Betriebsleistungskennzahl (OPI) (Sec.6.2.4; Leitlinien ISO 14031).

Notwendige Ressourcen (Infrastruktur, extern bereitgestellte Ressourcen, Informationssysteme, Kompetenz, Technik, finanzielle/personelle Ressourcen) zum Aufbau, zur Verwirklichung, Aufrechterhaltung und Verbesserung des UMS (Sec.7.1).
Notwendige Kompetenzen, um beabsichtigte Ergebnisse zu erreichen; Personen, deren Arbeit die Umweltleistung beeinflusst, sollten kompetent sein (Sec.7.2, Kasten 17).
Geeignete dokumentierte Information als Nachweis der Kompetenz aufbewahren (Sec.7.2, Schluss).
Wenn Kompetenz durch Schulung erworben wird: Schulungsbedarf ermitteln, Plan/Programm entwickeln, Schulungen durchfuehren, Ergebnisse bewerten, dokumentieren (Sec.7.2).
Personen unter Aufsicht der Organisation sind sich der Umweltpolitik, ihres Beitrags, der bedeutenden Umweltaspekte und der Konsequenzen von Abweichungen bewusst (Sec.7.3).
Festgelegte Prozesse fuer relevante Kommunikation: welche Informationen, wann/unter welchen Umstaenden, an wen, wie (Sec.7.4.1).
Interne (Sec.7.4.2) und externe (Sec.7.4.3) Kommunikation.

Aufrechtzuerhaltende/aufzubewahrende dokumentierte Information gemaess Kasten 19 (Anwendungsbereich, Politik, Aspekte, Verpflichtungen, Ziele, Steuerungen, Notfallprozesse, Kompetenz, Audit-/Bewertungsergebnisse usw.) (Sec.7.5.1).
Dokumentierte Information gelenkt: Kennzeichnung, regelmaessige Pruefung/Genehmigung, Verfuegbarkeit aktueller Versionen, Entfernen veralteter Information (Sec.7.5.2, 7.5.3).

Steuerung (Verfahren, Arbeitsanweisungen, technische Steuerung, kompetentes Personal) zur Steuerung bedeutender Umweltaspekte, Erfuellung bindender Verpflichtungen und Erreichen der Umweltziele (Sec.8.1.1-8.1.3).
Hierarchie zur Betrachtung von Steuerungen schaedlicher Umweltauswirkungen: Beseitigung, Ersatz, technische, verwaltungstechnische Steuerung (Sec.8.1.1).
Ausgewaehlte akzeptable Ablaufkriterien (z. B. Bedienungseigenschaften, Messungen von Gewicht/Temperatur), gegen die die Steuerung bewertet wird (Sec.8.1.3).

Plan, der den individuellen Erfordernissen entspricht; beruecksichtigt Gefahren vor Ort, Reaktionsmethoden, Verantwortlichkeiten, Fluchtwege, gegenseitige Hilfe, Kommunikation, Minderungsmassnahmen (Sec.8.2).
Regelmaessige Durchfuehrung von Notfalluebungen und periodisches Testen der Gefahrenabwehrverfahren (Sec.8.2).

label_de: Liste gefaehrlicher Stoffe mit moeglichen Umweltauswirkungen
label_en: List of hazardous materials with potential environmental impacts
description: Angaben zu gefaehrlichen Stoffen einschliesslich moeglicher Umweltauswirkungen und Massnahmen bei unfallbedingtem Freisetzen (Sec.8.2).

label_de: Ergebnisse von Ueberwachung, Messung, Analyse und Bewertung
label_en: Monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation results
description: Systematischer Ansatz fuer regelmaessige Ueberwachung/Messung/Analyse/Bewertung der Umweltleistung; bestimmt, was unter Beruecksichtigung von Zielen/Aspekten/Verpflichtungen/Steuerungen ueberwacht wird (Sec.9.1.1).

label_de: Ergebnis der Bewertung der Einhaltung bindender Verpflichtungen
description: Regelmaessige, iterative Bewertung, ob die Organisation ihre bindenden Verpflichtungen erfuellt; Nachweise aufbewahren (Sec.9.1.2).
Haeufigkeit/zeitliche Abstimmung je bindender Verpflichtung kann variieren; geeignet, um Wissen ueber den Einhaltungsstatus aktuell zu halten (Sec.9.1.2).
Programm zur Planung und Durchfuehrung interner Audits, basierend auf Art der Taetigkeiten, Umweltaspekten, Risiken/Chancen und vorausgegangenen Audits (Sec.9.2).
Ergebnisse interner Audits als Bericht; Nachweis der Verwirklichung des Auditprogramms und der Auditergebnisse aufbewahren (Sec.9.2).

Eingaben: Audit-/Einhaltungsergebnisse, Standpunkte interessierter Parteien, Umweltleistung, Zielerreichung, Status von Korrekturmassnahmen, sich aendernde Rahmenbedingungen, Ressourcen, Verbesserungsempfehlungen (Sec.9.3).

Entscheidungen zu Eignung/Angemessenheit/Wirksamkeit, fortlaufender Verbesserung, Ressourcenaenderungen, Massnahmen bei nicht erreichten Zielen, moeglichen Politik-/Zielaenderungen, Integration und strategischer Ausrichtung (Sec.9.3).
Aus Ueberwachung/Messung/Bewertung (9.1), Audits (9.2) und Managementbewertung (9.3) ermittelte Verbesserungsmoeglichkeit (Sec.10.1).
Nichterfuellung einer Anforderung in Bezug auf das UMS oder die Umweltleistung (Begriff 3.4.3, Sec.10.2).
Feststellung der Erfuellung (Konformitaet, Begriff 3.4.2) bzw. Nichterfuellung (Nichtkonformitaet, Begriff 3.4.3) einer Anforderung; Eingabe fuer Korrekturmassnahmen (Sec.10.2).
Nichtkonformitaet der UMS-Leistung oder der Umweltleistung (Beispiele verbatim Sec.10.2).
Untersuchung zur Bestimmung der Ursache(n), damit Korrekturmassnahmen auf den entsprechenden Teil des UMS konzentriert werden (Sec.10.2).

Massnahme zur Beseitigung der Ursache einer Nichtkonformitaet und zum Verhindern eines Wiederauftretens (Begriff 3.4.4); Art der Nichtkonformitaet und Ergebnisse als dokumentierte Information aufbewahren (Sec.10.2).
Bewertete und geplante Verbesserungsmassnahmen mit entsprechenden Aenderungen am UMS (Sec.10.3.1, 10.3.2).
Context in which the EDD assessment is carried out: during operations, or at the time of acquisition or divestiture of assets, or as part of a broader due-diligence process (§0.1).
The asset (organization, item or thing of potential or actual value) subject to the EDD assessment is identified, with its physical and/or organizational/intangible boundaries (§1, §3.4).
Whether the EDD assessment is a self-assessment/internal to the organization or an external assessment, with or without the need to employ third parties (§0.2).
Whether determination of business consequences is included; it is optional, at the discretion of the client (§3.11 Note 1; §5.5.3).
Whether conclusions are based on verified/validated objective information or, in its absence, on the assessor's professional judgement (§0.3).
EDD assessment evidence should be verifiable and/or validated; based on appropriate samples of the available information (§4.2.1).
A risk-based approach should be applied to planning, conducting and reporting so the assessment is focused on material matters and the objectives (§4.2.2).
The report should truthfully and accurately reflect the work performed, including limitations and changes to planned work, and be clearly presented (§4.2.3).
Information should not be used inappropriately for personal gain or detrimentally; sensitive/confidential information handled properly (§4.2.4).
Assessors should be honest, diligent and responsible; discreet in use/protection of information; impartial, fair and unbiased (§4.3.1).
Assessors should have and demonstrate the necessary competence and exercise due professional care and judgement, especially for qualitative information (§4.3.2).
Where an external assessor acts on behalf of a client, roles and responsibilities should be established formally (per 5.2.2-5.2.4); for internal assessment this guidance can assist (§5.2.1).

The client should determine the need for the assessment, define terms/objectives, determine and finalize scope and criteria, select assessor(s), give directions, define the division of work, approve the plan and provide authority/resources/information (§5.2.2 a-m).
The representative of the assessee should provide access to relevant areas and information, inform employees/parties, provide interviewees and assistance, and provide a safe workplace (§5.2.3 a-e).

label_en: Role of party to the assessment
description: Party to the assessment whose responsibilities are defined: client (5.2.2), representative of the assessee (5.2.3), assessor/team leader (5.2.4), assessment provider (5.2.5).

Indicator that the client, the assessor and the representative of the assessee are the same organization (self-assessment); for self-assessments the organization should ensure provider roles are addressed (§5.2.2, §5.2.5).

Assessment-provider roles (informed by ISO 19011) addressed: coordination/scheduling, programmes/methodologies/checklists/protocols, ensuring assessor competence and resources, and maintaining documented information (§5.2.5).
Criteria identified against which gathered information will be assessed (§5.3.4).

Category of criteria: applicable/foreseeable legal requirements, other client environmental requirements, requirements/claims of interested parties, technological requirements, or environmental issues established as material (§5.3.4).

The feasibility of the assessment determined to give reasonable confidence the objectives can be achieved (information, assessee cooperation, time/resources, on-site alternatives); a risk-based approach used to identify limitations (§5.3.5).

Where the assessor cannot physically visit the asset due to extraordinary events, alternatives to on-site assessment may be used (e.g. mobile video technology), noting their limitations and specialized techniques (§5.3.5).

Method selected for gathering information for the EDD depending on objectives/scope/criteria: questionnaires/surveys/checklists, personal interviews, documentation review, observation, focus-group discussions (§5.3.6).
Sampling technique used in information gathering: judgement-based or statistical sampling; quantitative and qualitative methods suitably determined (§5.3.6; §4.2.1).

An assessment plan prepared including (where applicable) parties, objectives & scope, criteria, priority areas, roles, working language, schedule, resources, procedure outline, reference documents, reporting and confidentiality requirements (§5.3.7).
The client should review and approve the assessment plan; it should be communicated to the representative of the assessee where appropriate (§5.3.7; §5.2.2 j).
The terms of the assessment confirmed with the assessor and the objectives specified by the client established before designing the assessment (§5.3.1, §5.3.2).

The scope establishing the boundaries and focus of the assessment defined, considering time/resources, objectives, existing information, client risk tolerance, relative priority and interested-party inputs (§5.3.3).

Type of boundary establishing the scope: physical (e.g. site, part of a site), organizational/intangible (contractors, suppliers, lessees, former occupants), or virtual (e.g. virtual data rooms) (§5.3.3; §0.2).
At the client's discretion the scope may be amended after the assessment begins; any change should be recorded and communicated to the relevant parties (§5.3.3).
The client may identify priority elements within the scope; identifying priorities does not exempt the assessor from taking the full scope into account (§5.3.3).
Information gathered on environmental aspects and related factors, consistent with the objectives/scope/plan and sufficient, relevant and accurate for the purpose (§5.4.1).
Documents and records collected and reviewed for a sufficient understanding of the asset without unnecessary duplication; findings corroborated from multiple sources (Annex A) (§5.4.2).
Working papers maintained recording the type, source, quality and reliability of information to support effective verification/validation (§5.4.2; §5.4.5).

Physical attributes and condition of the asset observed and recorded (activities; materials & properties; attributes/conditions of asset and surroundings -- Annex B), supported by photographic/written records where practicable (§5.4.3).
Category of observed physical attributes/conditions per Annex B: activities, materials and properties, attributes and conditions of the asset, attributes and conditions of the surroundings (§5.4.3).

Where the assessor is unable to gain access to any part of the asset, this limitation recorded in the assessment report; alternative sources (aerial photos, GIS, online research, fence-line) used where access is limited (§5.4.3).
The assessor should follow all applicable safety requirements when visiting/inspecting the asset (§5.4.3).
Interviews conducted (with client and assessee-representative approval) to corroborate/augment information from documents and observation; interviewees per Annex C (§5.4.4).

Category of interviewee per Annex C: internal (management, specialists, operators, maintenance), associated (legal advisors, contractors, suppliers, customers, investors, former occupants) or external (regulatory agencies, fire/emergency, municipal authorities, neighbours) (§5.4.4.2).
As information is gathered it should be verified and/or validated for accuracy, reliability, sufficiency and appropriateness for meeting the assessment objectives (§5.4.5; §3.21, §3.22).
The consequences of any information limitations determined and communicated to the client; valuable out-of-scope information also communicated (§5.4.5).
Environmental issues identified by comparing the verified/validated information with the selected criteria (liabilities/benefits, public-image effects, other risks and opportunities) (§5.5.2; §3.13).
Type of outcome identified for an environmental issue: liability or benefit to the organization, effect on the assessee's/client's public image, or other risk/opportunity (§5.5.2).

Business consequences (strategic/operational/economic/financial) of the identified/evaluated issues determined -- only if included in the objectives and scope; result is a list, quantified if appropriate (§5.5.3; §3.5).

Factor considered when exercising judgement on business consequences: environmental damage, scope of affected asset, current/future risks, reputation damage, policy nonconformance, environmental improvements, IP, estimated costs, technological developments/limitations, time period for costs (§5.5.3).
The assessor responsible for the report content; report provided as documented information presenting findings, their basis and the relative uncertainty associated with any finding (§6.1).

Report includes the should-be-reported content: assets assessed; assessor/author names; objectives, scope and criteria; dates and duration; information limitations and their consequences; limitations/exclusions/amendments/deviations from agreed scope; summary of information collected and results (§6.1).
The assessor should qualify any findings for which limitations exist, e.g. because of insufficient information (§6.1).
Reports are the sole property of the client; confidentiality respected and appropriately safeguarded by assessor(s) and recipients; distribution at the discretion of the client (§6.2).
All individuals undertaking EDD assessment activity have the Table 1 competencies plus prerequisite skills: language, note-taking/report-writing, presentation, ICT, interviewing (§7.1).
A suitable process applied for determining the competence needed; competence evaluated regularly and demonstrated before the individual takes responsibility for a particular EDD assessment (§7.2).
Area of competence from Table 1, classed as generic (necessary for each assessor) or specific (held by at least one team member) (§7.2, Table 1).

enum_values.label_en: Assessment criteria applicable to the scope

description: Whether a competence is generic (required of each assessor) or specific (held by at least one assessment-team member) (§7.2, Table 1).

The evaluation of assessor competence planned, implemented and documented (objective, consistent, fair, reliable) using the four-step process (determine required competence; establish criteria; select method; conduct evaluation), informed by ISO 19011 (§7.3).
Identifier of the engagement (arrangement between the V/V body and its client, usually a contract).
Whether the engagement is a validation (future outcomes), a verification (historical), or a mixed engagement.
Nature of the declared sustainability information; this document is applicable to quantitative and qualitative information (§1). Quantitative vs qualitative elaborated in §5.2.
Category of sustainability matter (attribute that can influence sustainability), per 3.1.1 Note 2 / 3.1.2.
The V/V body operates in accordance with ISO/IEC 17029 (Scope §1; normative reference §2; reinforced at §7.1.1).
Person or organization providing the declared sustainability information; retains responsibility for its accuracy and veracity.
Person or organization requesting validation/verification; can be the responsible party or the intended user.
Person or organization intended by the responsible party to use the declared sustainability information to make decisions for its stated purpose.
Person or organization responsible for developing and maintaining the V/V programme.
Body that performs validation (3.3.6) and/or verification (3.3.7).
Sustainability information declared by the responsible party; the object of conformity assessment in V/V.
Form/format in which the declared sustainability information is provided (3.1.4 Note 7).
Whether the declared information represents past results, current state or predicted future outcomes (3.1.4 Note 4).
Quantitative information (e.g. water consumption, injuries) vs qualitative information (e.g. narrative reports, strategy).

The V/V activity applied, depending on information type: quantitative (statistics, re-measurement/re-calculation, threshold comparison), qualitative (hypothesis testing, consistency, external review, judgement), computer/AI (confirm software functionality).
How quantitative/qualitative information was transformed (forecast: assumptions/limitations/methods; historical: summarizing, trends, visualization, combination, contextualization).
Access to raw data or the algorithms used to predict raw data is needed to see how the transformation was performed.
Whether outputs are digitally generated by computer or AI systems, including algorithms.
The responsible party applied the relevance determination process to decide what information is relevant to intended users.
If specific declared information is not under the responsible party's control, the responsible party specifies under whose control it resides and whether accuracy controls exist.
Whether the sustainability information is made available to parties external to the responsible party.
Conclusions are based on sufficient and appropriate objective evidence; the assurance opinion is based on evidence from an objective process.
Evidence can be based on sampling; sampling is undertaken appropriately to ensure confidence in the assurance opinion and the level of assurance.
The validator/verifier follows a consistent approach throughout the process.
The V/V process is documented and forms the basis for the conclusion and decision on assurance.
Decisions are based on objective evidence and not influenced by other interests or parties.
Identified threat to impartiality (self-interest, self-review, over-familiarity, intimidation).
Personnel have the necessary knowledge, skills, behaviours, experience, training, infrastructure and capacity.
Confidential and sensitive information is safeguarded and not inappropriately disclosed or used for personal gain.
Integrity demonstrated through honest, diligent, responsible behaviour observing legal provisions.
Activities, findings, conclusions, assurance and significant problems are truthfully and accurately reflected; unresolved/divergent views disclosed.
Due professional care, judgement and competence exercised in accordance with the risk attributed to the tasks.
Meaningful, accurate conclusions based on observations, knowledge, evidence and demonstration of professional scepticism.
The set of rules and procedures describing the declared sustainability information, identifying specified requirements & criteria and the V/V methodology.
Programme can be voluntary or mandatory (regulation or contractual requirements).
The programme includes all required elements (§7.1.2 a-f): description, specified requirements/criteria, planning/evidence criteria, decision rules, methodology/competence, deliverable category.
After evaluating suitability, the V/V body decides whether to proceed with validation/verification activities.
The declared sustainability information is clearly described (scope identification, format/media, consultation, intended users & purpose, disclosure, and historical/current/future specifics).
Applicable boundaries of the declared information (temporal, geographic, physical, economic, demographic or social).
Any consultation process performed by the responsible party (see Annex B).
The specified requirements (need/expectation stated) and criteria (reference against which information is validated/verified).
Identification of the declared information (with boundaries), the applicable programme, and the specified requirements & criteria.
The specified requirements and criteria are identified per §7.3.1 a-h (intended users, impacts/dependencies, suitability, disclosure, relevance, preconditions, references).
How the specified requirements and criteria are made available to intended users (publicly, within the information presentation, or within the assurance opinion).
Pre-engagement determination that the specified requirements and criteria are suitable; preconditions (relevance, completeness, reliability, neutrality, understandability).
At the engagement step, the V/V body agrees with the client the scope of V/V and the specified requirements and criteria.
Degree of confidence in the declared sustainability information; specified by the programme (e.g. reasonable, limited).
Materiality concept applied: misstatements that can influence the reliability of the information and decisions of intended users.
Overall process for risk identification, analysis, evaluation and mitigation (engagement/sampling/information risk).
A suitable methodology (or the programme-provided one) for performing V/V activities is identified.
Rules and procedures for the process steps (pre-engagement, engagement, planning, execution, review, decisions on nonconformities or post-issue facts).
Evidence-gathering activities, including techniques used remotely (e.g. drone surveys).
Category of deliverable as output of the V/V process (assurance statement/opinion or a non-assurance deliverable), per §7.5 c). Categories defined in Clause 6 and specified per §7.6.
Specific competence criteria for the V/V team (incl. technical experts) and independent reviewers per ISO 14019-4:2026 Annex A & Clause 4.
A competent person not in the V/V team who reviews the activities and conclusions (independent reviewer).
Requirements for the V/V body (e.g. governance, accreditation or designation by public authorities).
Whether a technical expert (specific knowledge on a sustainability matter; not acting as validator/verifier) supports the team.
Category of deliverable: assurance statements/opinions or non-assurance deliverables.
Declaration by the V/V body on assurance in accordance with an engagement agreement; based on validation/verification/mixed activities.
Conclusion type of the assurance opinion (unmodified, qualified, adverse, disclaimed).
Assurance information plus the assurance opinion.
Type of non-assurance deliverable (AUP report / report of factual findings, evidence report, findings report).

For a mixed engagement: strategic analysis/evidence plan and risk assessment separate validation from verification elements, and the deliverable explicitly states the separation and separate conclusions.
The V/V body and client agree the process to establish the deliverable and its format (category/format, process, nonconformity handling, corrections, references/distribution, post-issue facts).
How nonconformities (non-fulfilment of a specified requirement and criteria) are managed during V/V.
Validation should be undertaken by a validation body that uses ISO 14019-3.
Verification should be undertaken by a verification body that uses ISO 14019-2.
The validation/verification body conforms with ISO 14019-4 (normative reference).
Decision on whether the declared sustainability information conforms / is confirmed (with or without comments) per programme requirements.
A specific situation in which part of the V/V cannot be performed as intended (can affect conclusions, incl. disclaimed opinion).
Identifier of the organization, activity, facility, technology, product or system about which quantitative environmental information is acquired (§1, §4.1).
The actual application of the quantitative information, which sets the requirements of the objective (credibility, accuracy, transparency); lies outside the framework (§4.1, §6.1.1).

Whether the information is for internal use (§4.2), external use (§4.3) or for comparisons (§4.4); external and comparison uses set additional requirements on consistency, reliability and transparency.

Whether the information is intended for comparison (e.g. of systems over time, of system changes, or of different boundaries). If true, decisions must be generalizable and repeatable across the compared systems (§4.4, §6.2.2, §6.2.3).
Terms and definitions of ISO 14050 (Environmental management -- Vocabulary) apply per §2 in addition to Clause 3.
Classification of an information item per §3.1: basic data (3.1.1), activity data (3.1.2), quantitative data (3.1.3), quantitative information (3.1.4) or metadata (3.1.7).
Whether a datum is primary data (direct measurement or defined calculation thereon, 3.1.5/6.1.2.2.2) or secondary data (undefined calculation, modification, or any mix, 3.1.6/6.1.2.2.3).

Whether data represent a property of the foreground system (the subsystem of focus over which the user has control, 3.1.8/3.2.6) or the background system that lies outside it (3.1.9). Relate to a specific systems analysis, not to a data source (§6.1.2.4).

Whether data are specific (narrow applicability: site-, technology-, organization-, sector- or regionally specific) or generic (wide applicability). Determined by the requirements of the objective; does not imply data quality (§6.1.2.5).

A defined calculation method is an algorithm/mathematical function without secondary-data factors; an undefined calculation method is unknown, or known but uses secondary-data factors/parameters (§6.1.2.2.4).

Any means of acquiring data -- a defined measurement system (e.g. thermometer), copying a numerical value from a book/database, or an expert estimate; may provide primary or secondary data depending on choice (§6.1.2.3).

Sufficient metadata (measurement method, data gaps, scope of the system, etc.) should be supplied for each step and each intermediately produced datum so the information is reviewable, transparent and interpretable (§6.1.2.6, 3.1.7).
Selected data sources, system boundaries, measurement and assessment methods meet the requirements of the interested parties and/or the application (§5.2).
The quantitative environmental information provided is truthful, accurate and not misleading to interested parties (§5.3).
Compatible, coherent and non-self-contradictory data and information developed using recognized and reproducible methods and indicators respecting integrity constraints (§5.4).
Information generated, selected and provided in a consistent way with consistent measurement units, allowing comparisons (§5.5). Required where the application is a comparison.
Processes, procedures, methods, data sources and assumptions are made available to all relevant interested parties; volatility/uncertainty disclosed (§5.6).
All significant quantitative environmental information for the intended use is reflected such that no other relevant information needs to be added (§5.7).
Systematic errors and associated uncertainties minimized as far as practicable and bias towards a particular perspective eliminated (§5.8).
Information made relevant and fully understandable to interested parties using formats, language and media that meet their expectations and needs (§5.9).
Focus kept where it matters and where the information could influence the intended user's decisions; acceptable materiality determined by the application (§5.10).
The requirements of the objective set by the application -- the input to the process; the PDCA work process starts with Plan (§6.1.1, §6.2).
Conceptualization of the whole system: objective and intended use, the object, system boundaries, interested parties/target audience and general quality requirements (§6.2.1).
The boundaries of the system for which quantitative information is collected (§6.2.1).
Manageable components into which the object is divided (recursively, Figure 3); may be omitted if the system is simple (§6.2.2 NOTE). For comparison, components must be functionally comparable.

Quantifiable entities of a system component chosen to represent the quantified data -- requested by the objective or needed for calculations/aggregations (technical, ecological, socio-economic or other) (§6.2.3).

Category of selected parameter: technical (activity/production/geographical/energy/emission data), ecological (biodiversity/habitat/nutrient/biological), socio-economic (demographic/health/development/economic) or other (§6.2.3).

Definition of the basic data needed to quantify each parameter: which basic data, how it is transformed into the parameter value, and the scale of precision/statistical representativeness. Not needed if the parameter can be directly measured (§6.2.4 NOTE).
The required scale of precision and statistical representativeness for the basic data, set to fulfil the quantity and quality requirements of the objective (§6.2.4).

Description of how to acquire the basic data with the required precision/representativeness; depends on the object, property and required precision; selected from available standards, literature and/or expert advice (§6.2.5).
Data-quality assurance associated with metrological confirmation: establishing baselines, calibration, validation of the measuring system and verification of data collected (§6.2.5).

Implementation of the measurement planned in 6.2.5 (identify/adapt existing equipment, connect sensors). Significance of any deviation from Plan estimated and corrective values/routines applied if needed (§6.3.1).
Basic data acquired according to the measurement method (6.2.5). Failures/disturbances affect quality; their significance expressed as ranges or distributions of uncertainty (§6.3.2).
Estimation of the magnitude/significance of failures and disturbances of measurements, expressed in terms of ranges or distributions of uncertainty of the acquired basic data (§6.3.2, 3.3.3).
Parameters consolidated according to Plan (6.2.3); deviations explained with an estimation/evaluation/analysis of significance (qualitative leading to statistical uncertainty analysis) (§6.3.3).
Whether data processing/acquisition differed from Plan; if so the deviation is explained together with an estimation of its significance (§6.3.3, §6.3.4, §6.3.5).

Quantitative statements about subsystems formed by relating consolidated parameters to each system component (6.2.2); relationships established via mechanistic/physical/chemical relations, timeline synchronization, logic or other causalities (§6.3.4).
Quantitative statement of the total studied system, aggregated according to the objectives (6.2.1) and the appropriate aggregation type implied by the requirements of the objective (§6.3.5).
Quantitative measure of an activity that results in an environmental impact (3.1.2); the input multiplied by an emission/removal factor in the §6.2.3 c) 1) consolidation example.
Emission or removal factor by which activity data are multiplied to consolidate a parameter (§6.2.3 c) 1)); itself either primary or secondary data (§6.1.2.2.4).
Parameter value computed as activity_data * emission_removal_factor (Eq.1, §6.2.3 c) 1)); fed back into the consolidation/aggregation of the Do phase.

Check evaluates the actual correspondence between the tasks of Plan and Do and the overall meeting of the requirements of the objective; review checks that specifications are correct and were followed and results reported correctly (§6.4, §6.4.1).
Whether consistency is checked between each step throughout the procedure, enabling corrective measures before resources are spent on incorrect data and decisions (§6.4.2.1).
Form of Check/review applied: peer data-quality check, peer review or third-party review (§6.1.1, §6.4).
Each step of the Check stage is well-documented; review comments are documented and address the related Plan and Do documentation (§6.4.1).

Whether third-party review/verification is conducted; the framework supports peer and third-party review of resulting quantitative environmental reports (§6.4.2.2). Detailed V&V methods owned by the relevant verification standards (e.g. ISO 14064-3 for GHG).
Necessary actions taken to continually improve the acquisition and provision process based on the results of Check (§6.5).
The Act stage is well-documented since it may function as a work specification for future Plan and Do stages (§6.5).

label_en: Type of study (water footprint assessment / inventory study)
description: A water footprint assessment shall include the four LCA phases; a water footprint inventory study includes goal/scope, inventory analysis and interpretation (no impact assessment) and shall not be reported as a water footprint (§5.1).

label_en: Assessment mode (standalone / part of an LCA)
description: A water footprint assessment may be carried out and reported as a standalone assessment (water-related impacts only) or as part of an LCA (§5.1, §1).
Whether the assessment is for an organization, triggering the additional requirements and guidelines of Annex A (normative) (§5.1, Annex A).
The principles (§4.1-§4.13) are fundamental and shall be used as guidance for decisions on planning, conducting and reporting the water footprint assessment (§4.1).
The water footprint assessment considers all life-cycle stages as appropriate, from raw material to final disposal; may be restricted to one or more stages if justified (§4.2).

Whether the assessment is comprehensive. A comprehensive assessment yields a profile of impact-category indicator results and allows the unqualified term 'water footprint'; lack of data is not a justification to omit an important impact category (§5.1, §4.13).

When the assessment is not comprehensive, results shall be reported as a water footprint with a qualifier (e.g. 'availability water footprint', 'scarcity water footprint', 'eutrophication water footprint', 'non-comprehensive water footprint') (§5.1, §6.1).
Where relevant PCR exist they should be adopted provided they were developed per ISO 14025 and are considered appropriate (§5.1).
An organization shall consolidate its facilities' potential water-related impacts by either control or equity share; the chosen method shall be documented and any change explained (Annex A.2).

validation_rules.raw: is_organization_assessment  eq  true IMPLIES consolidation_method IN {control,equity_share}

description: The target audience (to whom the results are intended to be communicated) shall be unambiguously stated (§5.2.1).
The intended applications shall be unambiguously stated when defining the goal (§5.2.1).

label_en: Reasons for carrying out the study
description: The reasons for carrying out the study shall be unambiguously stated (§5.2.1).
Whether the study is part of an LCA where a comparative assertion intended for public disclosure is foreseen (§5.2.1). Triggers ISO 14044 requirements and a mandatory critical review (§6.3.1, §7.1).

Quantified performance of a product system, process or organization used as a reference unit (3.5.7); for organizations the term 'reporting unit' may replace 'functional unit'. Shall be considered and clearly described in the scope (§5.2.2 b).

Set of criteria specifying which unit processes are part of the product system or organization's activities (3.3.8); selection consistent with the goal; criteria identified and explained; documented (§5.2.2 a, §5.2.3).
For an organization, organization boundaries and system boundaries shall be determined and the applied consolidation method documented (§5.2.3, Annex A).
Definition and geographic coverage of the study shall be considered and clearly described (§5.2.2 c).
Definition and temporal coverage of the study shall be considered and clearly described (§5.2.2 c).
Specification of the material/energy flow amount or environmental-significance level for excluding unit processes/inputs/outputs (3.3.9); shall be considered and clearly described (§5.2.2 e).
Allocation procedures to be considered and clearly described in the scope (§5.2.2 f) and applied per the stepwise procedure of §5.3.3.2.
Water footprint impact assessment methodology and the selected impact categories shall be considered and clearly described in the scope (§5.2.2 h, see §5.4).
Whether the results will include an impact indicator result (and which), a water footprint profile, and/or a water footprint after weighting (§5.2.2 i, see §5.4.1).
Baseline conditions against which current conditions caused by the activities are compared, if applicable; may include the reference period and its inventory (§5.2.2 n, Note).
Type of report shall be considered and clearly described in the scope (§5.2.2 o, see Clause 6).
Type of critical review, if any, shall be considered and clearly described in the scope and the decision recorded (§5.2.2 p, §7.1, see Clause 7).

enum_values.label_en: Review by panel of interested parties

description: Quantities of water used (including water release and withdrawal) shall be considered for collection (§5.2.4.1 a, see §5.3.2).

Types of water resources used (incl. for withdrawal and for the receiving water body) shall be considered for collection (§5.2.4.1 b, see §5.3.2). Per flow these are picked from the water_resource_type categories (§5.3.2 b).
Data describing water quality (incl. for withdrawal, release and receiving water body) shall be considered for collection (§5.2.4.1 c, see §5.3.2).
Forms of water use shall be considered for collection (§5.2.4.1 d, see §5.3.2 d). Per flow these are picked from the form_of_water_use categories.

Locations of water use (incl. withdrawal, release or influence on water quality) required to determine area-related environmental condition indicators shall be considered for collection (§5.2.4.1 f, see §5.3.2).
Seasonal aspects in water flows, withdrawal and release, or water-quality changes, where relevant, shall be considered for collection (§5.2.4.1 g).
Temporal aspects of water use, including (where relevant) times of use and duration of water storage, shall be considered for collection (§5.2.4.1 h).

Data quality requirements should address: a) time coverage, b) geographic coverage, c) technology coverage, d) precision, e) completeness, f) representativeness, g) consistency, h) reproducibility, i) data sources, j) information uncertainty (§5.2.4.2 a-j).

Primary data should be collected when feasible; secondary data only used for inputs when primary collection is not possible/feasible, with reasons for significant processes justified and documented (§5.2.4.2).
The treatment of missing data shall be documented; assumptions stated as such with their basis described; the significance of missing data should be assessed (§5.2.4.3).
Water footprint results shall not include offsets (§5.2.5).

Quantity of water used per elementary flow: mass or volume (e.g. water inputs and water outputs) (§5.3.2 a). An elementary water flow is water entering the system withdrawn from the environment, or water leaving the system released to the environment (3.1.9).

Inventory calculations shall follow ISO 14044; all calculation procedures shall be documented explicitly and assumptions stated and explained, applied consistently throughout (§5.3.1 a, ISO 14044 §4.3.3).

Data validation shall be performed during collection to confirm the data-quality requirements are met; may include water mass balances and/or comparative analysis of water release factors (§5.3.1 b, ISO 14044 §4.3.3.2).

System-boundary adjustment shall be done per ISO 14044 §4.3.3.4 based on a sensitivity analysis to determine the significance of data; results of the adjustment and the sensitivity analysis shall be documented (§5.3.1 e).
The inventory shall include inputs and outputs for each unit process within the system; any discrepancy in the inventory balance shall be explained (§5.3.2).

label_en: Water resource type of the flow
description: Type of water resource used per elementary flow: rainwater; surface water; seawater; brackish water; groundwater (excluding fossil water); fossil water (§5.3.2 b).

label_en: Water quality parameters of the flow
description: Water-quality parameters/characteristics per elementary flow: physical (e.g. thermal), chemical and biological characteristics or functional descriptors of water quality (§5.3.2 c).

label_en: Form of water use of the flow
description: Forms of water use per elementary flow, e.g. evaporation; transpiration; integration in the product; release into a different watershed or the sea; displacement of water from one resource type to another within a watershed; instream use; other (§5.3.2 d).

enum_values.label_en: Release into a different watershed or the sea

description: Geographic location of water use or its effect (incl. withdrawal and/or release): site-specific information as needed, or assignment to a category from an appropriate watershed/region classification (§5.3.2 e).
Temporal aspects of water use per elementary flow, e.g. time of use and release if the relevant residence period occurs within the system boundary (§5.3.2 f).

label_en: Emissions to air and discharges to water/soil affecting water quality
description: Emissions to air and discharges to water and soil that impact water quality per elementary flow (§5.3.2 g). Emissions/discharges not affecting water quality are not included (§5.3.2 Note 2).
The sum of the allocated inputs and outputs of a unit process shall equal the inputs and outputs of the unit process before allocation (§5.3.3.1).
Where several alternative allocation procedures seem applicable, a sensitivity analysis shall be performed to illustrate the consequences of departing from the selected approach (§5.3.3.1).

Allocation procedure for reuse/recycling situations: closed-loop (allocation avoided; no change in inherent properties) or open-loop (material recycled into other systems with changed inherent properties) (§5.3.3.3).

Selected impact categories representing environmental issues to which LCI results are assigned (3.3.11); selected based on goal and scope; the method(s) and considered environmental mechanisms clearly described and documented (§5.4.2).
Quantifiable representation(s) of an impact category (3.3.12); the name shall be explicit about the environmental mechanism referred to and shall be documented accordingly (§5.4.2).

The characterization method/model to calculate the indicator results shall be identified and documented, including value choices and assumptions; it shall consider impacts due to change in water quantity and/or quality; choice explained and justified (§5.4.4.1).

Factor derived from a characterization model, applied to convert an assigned LCI result to the common unit of the category indicator (3.3.14) (§5.4.4.1). For scarcity, derived from models accounting for local differences in water scarcity (§5.4.5).

Life cycle inventory result assigned to an impact category in the classification step (§5.4.3); input to characterization (EQ-01). If the calculation is based on different impact categories, LCI results shall be assigned to those categories (§5.4.3).
The category indicator result: the assigned LCI results converted to common units via characterization factors and aggregated within the same impact category (output of EQ-01) (§5.4.4.1).
Collection of impact-category indicator results addressing potential water-related impacts (3.3.13); a non-comprehensive profile should be reported with a qualifier (§5.4.7).
Whether weighting is applied; if so it shall be performed and reported per ISO 14044, and weighted results shall not be the basis of a public comparative assertion (§5.4.7, §5.4.1).

Water issues are local; the impact assessment shall consider local conditions (watershed, precipitation, hydrology, climate, ecosystem, socio-economic) and, where relevant, seasonal/temporal aspects (§5.4.4.2).

Identification of the significant issues based on the results (e.g. processes with significant contribution, main environmental mechanisms affected, elementary flows with the greatest contribution) (§5.5 a).
The evaluation shall consider a completeness check (§5.5 b).
The evaluation shall consider a sensitivity check (§5.5 b); ISO 14044 §B.3.3 gives additional guidance (Note).
The evaluation shall consider a consistency check (§5.5 b).
Conclusions of the water footprint assessment (§5.5 d).
Limitations of the water footprint assessment (§5.5 e), reflecting the inherent limitations of a water footprint (§5.6).
Qualitative and/or quantitative assessment of uncertainty, e.g. by applying Monte Carlo simulation (§5.5 f).
The water footprint assessment and results shall be reported; results and conclusions reported fully, accurately and without bias, transparently and with sufficient detail (§6.1).

label_en: Water resource types & impacts explicit in report
description: The water resource types used and the potential water-related impacts addressed by the applied impact-assessment method(s) shall be explicit in the report (§6.1).

When results are reported to a third party, a third-party report shall be prepared covering aspects a)-g) (general aspects, goal, scope, inventory analysis, impact assessment where applicable, interpretation, critical review where applicable) (§6.2).

validation_rules.raw: report_type  eq  third_party IMPLIES third_party_report  eq  true

description: In a comparative study, the equivalence of the systems shall be assessed before interpretation; the same functional unit and equivalent methodological considerations shall be used and any differences identified and reported (§6.3.2).

A water footprint that is part of an LCA intended for a public comparative assertion shall be subject to a critical review applying the relevant ISO 14044 requirements (§7.1, §6.3.1). For other studies a critical review is not required but is possible (§7.1).

validation_rules.raw: comparative_assertion_public  eq  true IMPLIES critical_review_performed  eq  true

description: The critical review statement, the practitioner's comments and any responses to the reviewer's recommendations shall be included in the water footprint assessment report (§7.3, §7.4).
For a panel review, an independent external expert chairs a panel of at least three members; the chair selects other independent qualified reviewers (§7.4).

6.10 e) monitoring methodologies incl. estimation, modelling, measurement, calculation approaches and uncertainty.
6.10 f) monitoring frequency, considering intended-user needs.
6.10 g) roles & responsibilities incl. procedures to authorize, approve and document changes to recorded data.
6.10 h) controls incl. internal data checks for input, transformation and output, and corrective-action procedures.
6.10 i) GHG information management systems incl. location & retention of stored data and data-transfer procedures.
Where measurement and monitoring equipment is used, the proponent ensures calibrated or verified equipment is used and maintained appropriately.
Documentation demonstrating the GHG project's conformity with this document; consistent with verification & validation needs (6.12).
Where verification and/or validation is requested, it shall conform to the principles and requirements of ISO 14064-3.
GHG report prepared and made available to intended users; identifies intended use/user and uses a format/content consistent with intended-user needs.

For a public GHG statement claiming conformance: either a) an independent third-party ISO 14064-3 V&V statement, or b) a GHG report containing minimum content 6.13 b) 1)-15) (proponent name, project description, GHG statement of reductions/enhancements in CO2e, V&V statement, SSR list & selection criteria, project & baseline aggregated emissions/removals, baseline description & non-overestimation demonstration, criteria/procedures used, uncertainty statement, report date & period, permanence assessment, authorized-representative evidence, GHG programme(s), changes & conformity assessment).

Tipo de estudio: HCP (suma de emisiones y remociones de GEI de un sistema producto, expresada como CO2e por unidad funcional) o HCP parcial (uno o mas procesos seleccionados, por unidad declarada). Determina si se usa unidad funcional o declarada (3.1.1.1, 3.1.1.2, 5.3).
Aplicacion prevista del estudio de la HCP, declarada sin ambiguedad al definir el objetivo (6.3.1).

label_en: Reasons for carrying out the study
description: Razones para llevar a cabo el estudio de la HCP, declaradas sin ambiguedad (6.3.1).
Publico previsto del estudio de la HCP (6.3.1).
La comunicacion prevista, en su caso, de la HCP o informacion parcial de HCP, de acuerdo con la Norma ISO 14026 (6.3.1). La comunicacion en si esta fuera del alcance de este documento.
Si existe una RCP o HCP-RCP pertinente se debe adoptar. Pertinente si se desarrollo segun ISO/TS 14027, se ajusta a 6.3-6.5 y es adecuada para la organizacion (6.2).
Referencia y justificacion de la RCP/HCP-RCP adoptada; si hay mas de una pertinente, la eleccion debe estar justificada (6.2).
Un estudio de la HCP debe incluir las cuatro fases del ACV: definicion de objetivo y alcance (6.3), AICv (6.4), EICv (6.5) e interpretacion (6.6) (6.1).
La cuantificacion de la HCP considera todo el ciclo de vida: adquisicion de materia prima, diseno, produccion, transporte/entrega, uso y tratamiento al final de la vida util (5.2).

label_de: Relativer Ansatz / funktionelle o. deklarierte Einheit
description: El estudio se estructura alrededor de una unidad funcional (HCP) o declarada (HCP parcial) y los resultados se calculan en relacion con ella (5.3).
Se aplica un enfoque iterativo de reevaluacion al aplicar las cuatro fases del ACV (5.4).
Se da preferencia a las ciencias naturales en las decisiones; juicios de valor solo si no hay base cientifica ni convenciones internacionales (5.5).
Se incluyen todas las emisiones y remociones de GEI con contribucion significativa; el nivel de significancia lo determinan los criterios de corte (5.7, 6.3.4.3).
Se evita la doble contabilidad de emisiones y remociones de GEI dentro del sistema producto; cada una se asigna una sola vez (5.12, 6.4.6.1).
La HCP aborda una sola categoria de impacto: cambio climatico. Es una limitacion inherente (A.2, cap. 1); la HCP no deberia ser el unico componente de la decision.
Las consecuencias de las limitaciones de la HCP (categoria unica A.2 y metodologicas A.3) se deben reflejar en el informe del estudio de la HCP (Anexo A, 7.3).
El sistema en estudio y sus funciones, descritos al definir el alcance (6.3.2 a).
Alcance geografico del sistema en estudio, incluido en el limite del sistema (6.3.2 c).

label_en: No carbon offsetting in the CFP
description: La HCP y la HCP parcial no deben incluir la compensacion de carbono (6.3.4.1; 3.1.1.7). La compensacion y su comunicacion estan fuera del alcance.
Desempeno cuantificado del sistema producto usado como unidad de referencia (3.1.3.7). Debe definirse claramente y ser medible; usada en HCP completa (6.3.3).
Cantidad de producto usada como unidad de referencia en una HCP parcial (3.1.3.8). La unidad declarada solo se debe utilizar en una HCP parcial (6.3.3).

Medida de las entradas/salidas requeridas para cumplir la funcion expresada por la unidad funcional/declarada (3.1.3.9). Habiendo elegido la unidad, se debe definir el flujo de referencia asociado (6.3.3).
El limite del sistema debe ser la base para determinar que procesos unitarios se incluyen en el estudio de la HCP (6.3.4.1).
Cualquier exclusion de etapas, procesos, entradas o salidas solo se permite si no cambia significativamente las conclusiones; se debe declarar y explicar motivos e implicaciones (6.3.4.1).

Especificacion de la cantidad de flujo de materia/energia o nivel de significancia para excluir del estudio (3.1.4.1). Se deben definir criterios de corte coherentes; evaluar y describir su efecto en el informe (6.3.4.3).

Clasificacion de datos: especificos del sitio (primarios obtenidos dentro del sistema, 3.1.6.2), primarios (medicion directa o calculo basado en ella, 3.1.6.1) y secundarios (no cumplen requisitos de primarios, 3.1.6.3). Datos especificos del sitio para procesos bajo control y los mas importantes; secundarios solo cuando no es factible primario (6.3.5).
Los datos secundarios deben estar justificados y documentados con referencias en el informe del estudio de la HCP (6.3.5).

La calidad de los datos se debe caracterizar por aspectos cuantitativos y cualitativos: cobertura temporal, geografica y tecnologica, precision, integridad, representatividad, coherencia, reproducibilidad, fuentes e incertidumbre (6.3.5 a-j).
Enfoque en dos etapas: caracterizar los requisitos de calidad a)-d) y evaluar los datos respecto a esos requisitos (6.3.5).
Periodo de tiempo para el cual la cifra cuantificada de la HCP es representativa; se debe especificar y justificar (6.3.6).
Si la etapa de uso se incluye en el alcance, se deben incluir sus emisiones y remociones de GEI; especificar usuario y perfil de uso (6.3.7).

El perfil de uso debe especificarse; basarse en fuentes a)-e) (HCP-RCP, normas internacionales/nacionales/industria, patrones documentados); si no, definir supuestos y realizar analisis de sensibilidad (6.3.7).
Periodo durante el cual el producto en uso cumple los requisitos de desempeno (3.1.3.11). La informacion de vida util debe ser verificable y referirse a las condiciones de uso previstas (6.3.7).
Si la etapa de fin de vida se incluye en el alcance, se deben incluir todas sus emisiones y remociones de GEI (6.3.8).

Escenarios de fin de vida representativos del mercado actual y de las alternativas mas probables; supuestos basados en la mejor informacion y tecnologia actual, documentados (6.3.8). Procesos posibles a)-i).

label_en: Data collection for all unit processes
description: Se deben recopilar datos cualitativos y cuantitativos para todos los procesos unitarios incluidos en el sistema en estudio; documentar los procesos unitarios significativos (6.4.2).

Durante la recopilacion se debe realizar un control de validez (balances de masa/energia, comparacion de factores de emision) para evidenciar el cumplimiento de los requisitos de calidad de datos (6.4.3).
Determinar un flujo apropiado por proceso unitario y relacionar las entradas/salidas con el flujo de referencia y la unidad funcional/declarada (6.4.4).

Procedimiento de asignacion por pasos: Paso 1 evitar asignacion (subdivision/ampliacion del sistema); Paso 2 relacion fisica subyacente; Paso 3 otras relaciones (p.ej. valor economico) (6.4.6.2). La suma de las entradas/salidas asignadas debe igualar a las del proceso antes de la asignacion (6.4.6.1).
La suma de las entradas y salidas asignadas de un proceso unitario debe ser igual a las entradas y salidas del proceso unitario antes de la asignacion (6.4.6.1).

Si se usa la HCP para seguimiento del desempeno: evaluaciones en distintos momentos, misma unidad funcional/declarada, mismo metodo/RCP/factores de caracterizacion; periodo entre evaluaciones no menor que el limite de tiempo de los datos (6.4.7).

label_en: Timing of GHG occurring >10 years specified
description: Todas las emisiones/remociones de GEI se calculan como si ocurrieran al inicio del periodo. Si las de uso o fin de vida ocurren >10 anos despues del uso (salvo otra cosa en la RCP), se debe especificar su momento en el inventario; el efecto del calendario, si se calcula, se documenta por separado (6.4.8).
Las emisiones y remociones de GEI de los fosiles se deben incluir en la HCP/HCP parcial y documentar por separado como resultado neto (6.4.9.2; Tabla 1: X debe estar incluido).
Las emisiones y remociones biogenicas de GEI se deben incluir en la HCP/HCP parcial y deberian expresarse por separado (6.4.9.2; Tabla 1).

Si se calcula, el contenido de carbono biogenico del producto se documenta por separado pero NO se incluye en el resultado de la HCP/HCP parcial; se debe proporcionar en estudios de la cuna a la puerta (6.4.9.3).

Tratamiento de la electricidad: generada internamente (6.4.9.4.2), de proveedor conectado directamente (6.4.9.4.3), producto electrico especifico del proveedor o promedio de la red pertinente (6.4.9.4.4), incluyendo emisiones aguas arriba, generacion+perdidas T&D y aguas abajo; evitando doble contabilidad (6.4.9.4.1, 5.12).

label_en: GHG from direct land use change (dLUC)
description: Las emisiones y remociones de GEI por CUS directo se deben evaluar segun metodos reconocidos (p.ej. Directrices IPCC) e incluir en la HCP; las netas de CUS se documentan por separado (6.4.9.5; Tabla 1: X debe estar incluido).

El cambio de uso del suelo indirecto (CUSi) se deberia incluir una vez exista un procedimiento acordado internacionalmente; debe ser considerado para inclusion y, si se calcula, documentado por separado (6.4.9.5; Tabla 1).

Las emisiones y remociones de GEI por uso del suelo (cambios en reservas de carbono no derivados de CUS) se deberian evaluar e incluir; si no, justificar; cuando se incluyan, documentar por separado (6.4.9.6).

Las emisiones de GEI del transporte aereo se deben incluir en la HCP y documentar por separado; si se usa un multiplicador de aviacion, su efecto no se incluye en la HCP y se notifica por separado con la fuente (6.4.9.7).

label_en: GHG emissions of primary raw-material acquisition
description: Emisiones ligadas a la extraccion o produccion de las materias primas necesarias para el producto, como si fueran todas materiales primarios (formula D.1, Anexo D informativo).
Emisiones ligadas a las operaciones de fin de vida (parte del sistema producto que entrega el material reciclado) (formula D.1, Anexo D informativo).
Indice de reciclado del material; R*E_V es el credito de reciclado (formula D.1, Anexo D informativo).

Emisiones de GEI ligadas a la adquisicion de materias primas y operaciones de fin de vida en asignacion de ciclo cerrado, con credito de reciclado (formula D.1: E_M = E_V + E_EoL - R*E_V). Anexo D INFORMATIVO.

Indice de asignacion para el reciclado en ciclo abierto; relacion entre el precio de mercado del material de desecho/reciclado y el del material primario. A=1 si igual valor de mercado; A=0 si el material reciclado se entrega gratis (sin credito de reciclado). Ejemplo arbitrario A=0,5. (Anexo D, D.4; formulas D.2-D.6, informativo).
Contenido reciclado del producto, usado en las formulas de reciclado de ciclo abierto para productos compuestos de material primario y reciclado (Anexo D, D.4; formulas D.5/D.6, informativo).

label_en: GHG of pre-processing of recycled material
description: Emisiones de GEI ligadas al pre-procesamiento del material reciclado para cumplir los requisitos de calidad del material primario sustituido (Anexo D, D.4; formulas D.3-D.6, informativo).

Emisiones de GEI ligadas a la adquisicion de materias primas y operaciones de fin de vida en reciclado de ciclo abierto cuando el producto es 100% material primario (formula D.2: E_M = E_V + E_EoL - R*A*E_V). Anexo D, D.4, INFORMATIVO.
Emisiones de GEI en reciclado de ciclo abierto, producto 100% material reciclado (formula D.3: E_M = E_V*A + E_PP + E_EoL - R*A*E_V). Anexo D, D.4, INFORMATIVO.
Emisiones de GEI en reciclado de ciclo abierto, producto 100% material reciclado, alternativa a D.3 (formula D.4: E_M = E_PP + E_EoL + (1-R)*A*E_V). Anexo D, D.4, INFORMATIVO.
Emisiones de GEI en reciclado de ciclo abierto, producto de material primario y reciclado (formula D.5: E_M = C*A*E_V + C*E_PP + (1-C)*E_V + E_EoL - R*A*E_V). Anexo D, D.4, INFORMATIVO.
Emisiones de GEI en reciclado de ciclo abierto, producto de material primario y reciclado, alternativa a D.5 (formula D.6: E_M = C*E_PP + (1-C)*E_V + E_EoL + (C-R)*A*E_V). Anexo D, D.4, INFORMATIVO.

Masa de cada GEI liberado o eliminado por el sistema producto, por gas (entrada al calculo de impacto, de la hoja 04). Para CO2 biogenico se caracteriza como -1 (remocion) o +1 (emision) kg CO2e/kg CO2 (6.5.1, 6.5.2).

Potencial de calentamiento global a 100 anos proporcionado por el IPCC (con retroalimentacion de carbono), en kg CO2e por kg de emision; factor de caracterizacion. Se deben usar los ultimos valores del IPCC salvo justificacion (6.5.1; 3.1.2.4).
Resultado de la HCP o HCP parcial: suma de los impactos de cada GEI (masa * PCG100), expresado en masa de CO2e por unidad funcional o declarada (6.5.1, NOTA 1; 7.2). Producido por EQ-01.
El PCG para otros horizontes temporales y el PCTG (GTP), segun el IPCC, se pueden usar ademas del PCG100, pero se deben informar por separado (6.5.1).

Las remociones de CO2 en biomasa se caracterizan como -1 kg CO2e/kg CO2 al ingresar al sistema; las emisiones de CO2 biogenico como +1 kg CO2e/kg CO2 (6.5.2). Para metano fosil y biogenico, factores del informe IPCC mas reciente.
Identificacion de las cuestiones importantes sobre la base de los resultados de AICv y EICv (etapas, procesos o flujos) (6.6 a).
Evaluacion que considera la integridad, la coherencia y el analisis de sensibilidad (6.6 b).
Formulacion de conclusiones, limitaciones y recomendaciones (6.6 c).
La interpretacion debe incluir una evaluacion de la incertidumbre, incluida la aplicacion de reglas o intervalos de redondeo (6.6).

La interpretacion deberia incluir analisis de sensibilidad de entradas, salidas y opciones metodologicas significativas (incl. asignacion), e influencia de perfiles de uso y escenarios de fin de vida alternativos (6.6).

Se debe elaborar el informe del estudio de la HCP, que describe el estudio (incluida la HCP/HCP parcial) y demuestra el cumplimiento de la norma; resultados sin sesgo, transparentes y con suficiente detalle (7.1).
Los resultados de la HCP/HCP parcial se deben documentar en masa de CO2e por unidad funcional o declarada (7.2).

Se deben documentar por separado: emisiones/remociones por etapa principal (contribucion absoluta y relativa), GEI fosiles netas, biogenicas, CUSd y aeronaves; y si se calculan: CUSi, uso del suelo, sensibilidad de la red, carbono biogenico de productos y la HCP con PCG100 (7.2 a-e).

label_en: List of GHG taken into account
description: La lista de GEI tomada en cuenta se debe incluir en el informe (7.3 e). Para la lista de GEI consultar el ultimo informe del IPCC (3.1.2.1 NOTA 1).
Los factores de caracterizacion seleccionados (PCG) se deben incluir en el informe (7.3 f).

El informe debe incluir la informacion requerida 7.3 a)-t): unidad funcional/flujo de referencia, limite del sistema, procesos importantes, recopilacion de datos, lista de GEI, factores de caracterizacion, criterios de corte, asignacion, momento de GEI, descripcion y calidad de datos, sensibilidad/incertidumbre, electricidad, interpretacion, opciones de valor, alcance, etapas, periodo representativo, RCP y seguimiento (7.3).
El tratamiento de la electricidad debe incluir informacion sobre el calculo del factor de emision de la red y las restricciones especificas de la red (7.3 l).
Informacion opcional para el informe: conformidad con el Anexo B y presentacion grafica de los resultados (7.4 a-b).

Si se realiza una comparacion basada en la HCP, se deben cumplir los requisitos del Anexo B (normativo): mismos requisitos de cuantificacion, ciclo de vida completo (salvo HCP parcial con procesos omitidos identicos), misma HCP-RCP, criterios a)-i) y criterios de ICV/EICV identicos/equivalentes.

Si una organizacion desarrolla un enfoque sistematico de HCP debe cumplir el Anexo C (normativo): descripcion del enfoque, recursos/competencias/infraestructura, capacidad de producir la HCP de un producto conforme a la norma, gestion de riesgos de obsolescencia y procedimiento documentado (C.2-C.4).

Tipo de revision critica, en su caso (6.3.2 k). Se debe realizar conforme a la Especificacion Tecnica ISO/TS 14071 cuando corresponda (cap. 8); facilita la comprension y mejora la credibilidad de la HCP.
Name/identification of the financial institution (or other user) applying the framework.
Type of user of the standard or of the information it produces: financial institution, climate policymaker, or financial authority.

Which of the four support functions the standard provides to investors: harmonizing definitions/concepts/frameworks; identifying relevant climate actions; providing reporting & communication requirements/guidance; providing a measurement framework linking financial activity to real-economy impact.

The fundamental climate-related objective pursued: managing climate-related financial risks & opportunities, contributing to climate goals, or both. Determines the relevant approaches, metrics, tools and actions.
Confirmation that the objective is clearly identified rather than mixing risk management and contribution without clear expected outcomes.
Confirmation that KPIs measuring the results of an action are specific to the pursued objective (consistent process: identify actions -> define KPIs -> set & track target).
One of the seven landscape concepts identified across financial-institution narratives (Fig.1).
Whether the climate action/initiative is individual (single FI) or cooperative (coalition of FIs).
Core financial function; the WG focuses on investment-portfolio and loan-book management functions (other services addressed at a second stage).
Whether the function is within the WG's initial scope (investment-portfolio / loan-book management); non-finance-specific actions (lobbying, operational GHG) are excluded.
Asset class to which a climate-related action applies (action library by asset class).
Specific climate-related action from the illustrative action library (to become a 'library' of climate-related actions).

The way an action links to risk management: limit exposure to riskier assets; increase exposure to undervalued opportunities; influence investee mitigation by setting conditions; hedge via a reverse-correlated instrument.
Type of climate-related risk factor considered (per the PCI Carbon Asset Risk framework risk factors and Section 3.5.2): policy/legal, technology, market/economic, reputational, physical, litigation.

The way an action contributes to climate goals: limit exposure to misaligned activities (raise their cost of capital); increase exposure to activities that must expand; shareholder engagement / conditionality / signalling to influence investee decisions.
Whether a 'pathway to impact' on GHG emissions has been defined for the action, including order of magnitude and conditions for success.
Pre-defined category of an action's climate-impact potential (high/medium/low), based on order-of-magnitude outcomes and conditions for success.
Kind of metric: exposure metric (e.g. green/brown share, carbon intensity), genuine climate-impact metric (physical-asset-level), or value-at-risk metric.
Level at which the climate-impact indicator is tracked; the recommended level is physical-asset-level to avoid portfolio-turnover and issuer-scope accounting effects.
Whether misleading accounting effects are controlled: investment-portfolio turnover (level 1), change of activities due to M&A (level 2), and volatile denominators (e.g. CO2/$ of sales).
Genuine value-at-risk based on the sensitivity of valuation and creditworthiness to an adverse climate scenario (not a proxy exposure indicator).
Position in the climate-risk transfer chain where a risk may or may not be material (society, physical-asset owner, security issuer, security owner, financial system as a whole).
Climate scenario used; for the contribution objective only a well-below-2C / 2C scenario is generally useful (long-term global scenario), otherwise local/short-term scenarios apply.
Scenario time frame, which should be consistent with the financial exposure / investment horizon.
Whether key scenario factors/assumptions are documented: risk factors (policy, technology, market), current & likely-to-be-enacted policies, demand assumptions, scope, ambition, uncertainty.
Whether the investor's 'starting point'/baseline (alignment vs climate goals) has been established as a basis for target-setting and progress measurement.

Whether the well-below-2C macro-economic target has been 'translated' into an indicative benchmark/target for financial assets (burden-sharing rules, time frames). The macro-to-asset translation is the WG10 conclusion topic 'consistency with climate goals' (p.45/p.47).
Staged scope of the standard: stage 1 = framework to assess contribution to the Paris Agreement; stage 2 = framework for managing climate-related risks.
Topic prioritised for the future standard (management/disclosure of processes, outcomes of actions, value-at-risk, scenario design/translation, exposure assessment).
Whether a relevant, actionable climate-related target (contribution or risk) has been set and is being managed/tracked.
External and internal issues relevant to the organization's purpose and ability to achieve intended WEMS outcomes.
Interested parties relevant to the water efficiency management system.
Relevant requirements of the interested parties.
Boundaries and applicability of the WEMS; shall be available as documented information.
Confirmation that the WEMS is established, implemented, maintained and continually improved incl. processes and interactions.
Top management demonstrates leadership and commitment via the actions of §5.1 a)-k).
Documented water efficiency policy meeting §5.2 a)-h); communicated and available to interested parties (3.35).
Responsibilities and authorities for relevant roles assigned and communicated (§5.3 a)-d)).

label_en: Management representative / person(s) for water efficiency
